question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x-2}{4-{x}^{2}},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $
question.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+3x-2}{4-{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{(x+2)(2x-1)}{(x-2)(x+2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is  $x\ne \pm 2,$ and we notice that the function can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=-\frac{2x-1}{x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we see that the function has the only vertical asymptote $x=2.$ So statement II is false.

To find  ${lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=2$ from the left and right.

| $x$ | $1.99$ | $1.999$ | $2$ | $2.001$ | $2.01$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $298$ | $2\,998$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $-3\,002$ | $-302$ |

All values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to 2$ from the left and all values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to 2$ from the right . Therefore, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty \,{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x)=\infty 
$$

Consequently, statement I is true and III is false.

In conclusion, only statement I is correct. A plot of the function is shown below.
